steps.title: NOSIH
steps.body: A decentralised registry of land deeds. Records are written to Polygon Amoy; the documents stay encrypted and off-chain.

steps.title: Sign in
steps.body: Registrar accounts only. The token is issued here and held for the session — it never leaves the browser.

steps.title: Public verification
steps.body: No account needed. Anyone with a Land ID can check who owns a parcel and whether the record still matches the chain.

steps.title: What happens next
steps.body: Four steps take you through the whole system: register a deed, watch the registry, open the records table, then verify a parcel as a stranger would.

steps.title: The registry at a glance
steps.body: Every deed is anchored on-chain and mirrored in an access-controlled database. This page is the registrar's view of both.

steps.title: Live counters
steps.body: Parcels, records, transfers and revocations, read from the database on every load. They are never cached.

steps.title: Recent records
steps.body: The five most recent registrations. A Land ID here is the permanent identity of a parcel — it survives every later transfer.

steps.title: Register a deed
steps.body: Upload the signed PDF. The server reads it, encrypts it, pins it, and writes only hashes and owner IDs to the chain.

steps.title: Search the registry
steps.body: Search by Land ID, record, survey number, village or owner. Open a deed, download its QR, or revoke it.

steps.title: Verify as the public
steps.body: The same view a citizen sees: an ownership timeline with no registrar login, cross-checked against the chain on every request.

steps.title: Your session
steps.body: The signed-in registrar and their role. Sign out clears the token from this tab only.

steps.title: Start with the document
steps.body: Drop the registered deed PDF. AI reads the survey number, boundaries and registration details, and pre-fills the form — every field stays editable.

steps.title: The parcel identity
steps.body: The Land ID is derived from jurisdiction, survey number and subdivision. The same parcel always derives the same Land ID, whatever the owner.

steps.title: Linking to an existing parcel
steps.body: When the Land ID already exists, the new deed becomes the next record in that chain and inherits the previous owner automatically.

steps.title: Parties
steps.body: Buyer and seller. Names stay in the database; the chain only ever sees keyed hashes and registry IDs like OWN-31E19C9D.

steps.title: Location
steps.body: State, district, taluk, village and survey number. Together they derive the jurisdiction code and the Land ID.

steps.title: Land details and registration
steps.body: Area and boundaries, document type, registration number, date and the sub-registrar office.

steps.title: What actually goes on-chain
steps.body: Only hashes, the encrypted file's CID and owner registry IDs. Names, survey numbers and boundaries stay in the access-controlled database.

steps.title: The receipt
steps.body: A QR code for the parcel, the Land ID and Record ID, the transaction on Amoy, the document hash and the encrypted CID.

steps.title: The QR code
steps.body: Scanning it opens the public verification page for that exact parcel. It is the handoff from registrar to citizen.

steps.title: Search
steps.body: One box across Land ID, record ID, survey number, village and owner name.

steps.title: Current records only
steps.body: Off shows the full history of every parcel. On shows only the head of each chain.

steps.title: The registry table
steps.body: Land ID, record, owner, location, document, status. Every row is cross-checkable against the contract.

steps.title: Status
steps.body: ACTIVE or REVOKED. Revocation is recorded on-chain; the record stays visible forever.

steps.title: Verify
steps.body: Opens the public verification page for that parcel.

steps.title: Open the original
steps.body: Decrypts the stored PDF for this registrar and opens it. The hash is checked against the chain on the way out.

steps.title: Download QR
steps.body: The same QR the citizen would scan.

steps.title: Revoke
steps.body: Permanently marks the record revoked on-chain. It requires a written reason, which is recorded on the ledger.

steps.title: Paging
steps.body: Server-side paging, so the registry stays responsive with thousands of records.

steps.title: Enter a Land ID
steps.body: The only field on the public page. A Land ID is in the QR code on the deed itself, so a citizen can check their own parcel without asking anyone.

steps.title: The verdict
steps.body: REGISTERED LAND RECORD only appears when the database and the contract agree. A revoked record says so; an unknown ID says so.

steps.title: The parcel
steps.body: Location, jurisdiction code, current record and current owner ID. Owner names are deliberately not published.

steps.title: The parcel's QR
steps.body: The public face of the parcel, rendered on demand by the API.

steps.title: Ownership history
steps.body: Every transfer, newest first, with the owner ID it moved to and the owner ID it moved from.

steps.title: On-chain match
steps.body: The record was re-read from the contract just now and matches the database. This check runs on every visit, not on a cached copy.

steps.title: Proof data
steps.body: The document hash, the previous-record hash, the encrypted CID and the moment of registration.

steps.title: Check a deed PDF
steps.body: Anyone can drop their own copy of a deed. It is hashed and compared with the registered versions — and never stored.

steps.title: What a match proves
steps.body: A matching hash proves the file is the one that was registered. It does not by itself prove legal ownership or the validity of the transaction.

steps.title: View the original
steps.body: The encrypted file is fetched from IPFS and decrypted on the server, then its hash is compared with the one recorded on the blockchain. A match proves this is the very document that was registered.
